channel.title: Farmer's Weekly SA - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Farmer's Weekly SA (farmersweekly.co.za)

item.title: Western Cape ramps up efforts to combat foot-and-mouth disease
item.description: The Western Cape is on high alert following suspected and confirmed outbreaks of foot-and-mouth disease in three informal settlements and on one commercial dairy farm.

item.title: Foot-and-mouth disease explained
item.description: As foot-and-mouth disease continues to wreak havoc in South Africa, with misinformation circulating and anxiety growing among farmers, Farmer’s Weekly approached Dr Dave Midgley, CEO of the Ruminant Veterinary Association of South Africa, to answer the questions farmers on the ground are asking.

item.title: FMD in SA: no cloven-hoofed animals at Nampo 2026
item.description: Organisers of South Africa’s largest agricultural exhibition have confirmed that no cloven-hoofed animals will be exhibited at the 2026 Nampo Harvest Day, scheduled for 12 to 15 May at Nampo Park in Bothaville in the Free State.

item.title: World Pulses Day highlights the untapped potential of pulses
item.description: Building on the success of the International Year of Pulses in 2016, led by the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), 10 February was designated as World Pulses Day, to be commemorated each year.

item.title: MEC Elzabe Rockman details Free State’s FMD containment plan
item.description: At an engagement session hosted by the Free State Department of Agriculture and Rural Development at the Harry Gwala Multi-Purpose Hall in Sasolburg on 5 February, MEC Elzabe Rockman outlined the province’s foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) response plan to Farmer's Weekly's Gary Wium.

item.title: Animal feed industry enters recovery phase
item.description: Data from the Animal Feed Manufacturers Association (AFMA), the recognised representative body of South Africa’s formal animal feed industry, show that the industry entered a clear recovery phase in 2025 after contracting in 2024.

item.title: South Korea added to export roster for SA table grapes
item.description: The export protocol allowing South African table grapes to be shipped to the Republic of Korea (South Korea) was finalised late last month, paving the way for exports to begin in the 2026/27 season.

item.title: Getting to the root of healthy vineyards
item.description: Vineyard success is built from the ground up, starting with the correct planting and care of new vines. Glenneis Kriel reports on the advice of viticulturist Marko Roux on how growers can give vines the best possible start.

item.title: Call for VAT-free chicken ahead of 2026 Budget Speech
item.description: Civil society organisation FairPlay has renewed its call for VAT-free chicken ahead of Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana’s Budget speech later this month, saying zero-rating basic poultry products would be the fastest way to address food insecurity and child malnutrition in South Africa.

item.title: The story of the Drakensberger beef cattle breed’s evolution in Africa
item.description: The Drakensberger cattle breed has been part of the South African landscape for ages. So-called black indigenous cattle existed in South Africa as early as the 15th and 16th centuries and formed the foundation of the current Drakensberger beef cattle breed.
